text.p: Troubled Mexican conglomerate Grupo Sidek on Thursday released its audited results from 1996 showing lower revenues but also a lower net loss and a lower negative equity compared to 1995.
"Net losses from 1996 were 3.039 million pesos compared to a net loss of 4.125 million pesos in (1995)," Sidek said in a statement.
Revenues fell by 13 percent to 4.310 billion pesos in 1996 from 4.952 billion pesos in 1995, the statement said.
Sidek originally reported 1996 revenues of 4.322 billion pesos with a net loss of 2.428 billion pesos.
The audited results were released with less than a month to go before the June 30 deadline for Sidek, which on the verge of dissolution, to present a restructuring plan to creditors.
The company's balance sheet is so poor that it was delisted from the New York Stock Exchange earlier this year.
Sidek reported a total debt of 23.228 billion pesos at the end of 1996, down six percent from the total debt of 23.539 percent at the end of 1995.
The level of negative equity also improved in 1996, falling to 1.980 billion pesos versus 3.447 billion pesos in 1995.

Situr, the tourism subsidiary, posted revenues 21 percent lower in 1996 from 1995, while Simec, the steel unit, showed revenue gains of four percent in 1996, rising to 2.182 billion pesos from 2.108 billion in 1995.

"In Simec, the production of billet steel increased 6.6 percent, calling attention to the increase of 12 percent in the Mexicali plant," the report said, adding that the Mexicali and Guadalajara plants operated at a combined 89 percent of capacity.. ((--Monica Ballesca, Guadalajara bureau, +523 817-0397))
